title: MotifDefinition
description: Ordered/typed edge-pattern sequence + completion condition + time bound for a single cached motif (tasks.md 3.1, specs.md FR3.1/FR3.5/§7 'Motif Definition'). One instance of this shape per entry under config/motifs.yaml's top-level `motifs` map; the map key is the motif's name.

description.description: Human-readable summary of the attack pattern this motif represents.

window_seconds.description: Completion time bound: the motif resets if the gap between its first matched edge and its final matched edge exceeds this many seconds (specs.md FR3.1's '~4 hours' example).

steps.description: Ordered sequence of edge patterns. Step 0 starts a new candidate chain; each subsequent step must match an edge that extends an existing chain's entity binding (see `key_field`/`key_resolver`). The motif completes when the final step matches.

edge_type.description: Edge type(s) this step accepts. Omit/null to match any edge_type.

protocol.description: Protocol(s) this step accepts. Omit/null to match any protocol.

src_type.description: Node type(s) this step's src must have. Omit/null to match any src_type.

dst_type.description: Node type(s) this step's dst must have. Omit/null to match any dst_type.

key_field.description: Which endpoint of an edge matching this step carries the chain's entity-binding key: at step 0 this endpoint's id becomes the new chain's key; at later steps this endpoint must resolve (via key_resolver) to the chain's existing key.

key_resolver.description: How to test whether key_field's endpoint continues the chain. 'identity': the endpoint id must literally equal the chain key. 'host_admin': the endpoint (a User) is treated as the admin/service account of the chain key (a Machine) via a documented naming-convention heuristic -- see motifs.py.
